almanac.about:
CentralAsiaCiv draws the five republics of Central Asia — Uzbekistan, Kazakhstan, Kyrgyzstan, Tajikistan and Turkmenistan — like a 4X strategy game map, inspired by Andrej Karpathy's usaciv and EarthCiv.

How it's built

All five republics are projected in Albers Equal-Area Conic centered on 67°E, 45°N and cut into 80×73 hexes, each 50 km corner to corner (25 km radius). Real elevation from NOAA ETOPO1 raises the 7,000 m Pamirs and Tian Shan and carves the Caspian Sea basin, while NASA MODIS satellite imagery paints the Kyzylkum and Karakum deserts, the Kazakh Steppe, the Altai forests and the irrigated Fergana and Zarafshan oases.

Controls

Drag or WASD / arrow keys to pan · scroll or +/− to zoom · click any city for its City View (citizens & districts), or click any republic for its national profile · open Advisors for 10 interactive dashboards · / to search · L to cycle lenses · R to toggle resources · ? for shortcuts.
almanac.regions: Click any land hex to inspect its republic (Uzbekistan, Kazakhstan, Kyrgyzstan, Tajikistan or Turkmenistan). National population, GDP, growth and unemployment come from World Bank WDI 2025; sub-national lenses map all 48 provinces (viloyats, oblystar, oblasts and welayats).
almanac.lenses_intro: Sixteen lenses color all 48 Central Asian provinces and hexes by population density, 2021–25 growth, median age, household income, GDP per capita, poverty, homeownership, degrees, internet access, commute, faith, natural hazards and NASA MODIS land cover.
almanac.resources_intro: Resource icons show power plants ≥ 25 MW (WRI Global Power Plant Database + newly commissioned solar, wind & hydro projects) alongside flagship mines (Muruntau gold, Almalyk & Aktogay copper, Chu-Sarysu & Uchkuduk uranium, Bogatyr coal) and supergiant oil & gas basins (Tengiz, Kashagan, Galkynysh, Shurtan).
almanac.beyond_borders: Neighboring Eurasia (Russia, China, Afghanistan, Iran, Azerbaijan & Mongolia) is shaded for geographic context.
advisor.council.note: All 10 Advisors slice real public data across Uzbekistan, Kazakhstan, Kyrgyzstan, Tajikistan & Turkmenistan: World Bank WDI 2025, Natural Earth, NOAA ETOPO1, NASA MODIS, WRI Power Plants, OurAirports, UNESCO and national statistical yearbooks.
